subject: NeuroRetail dedicated pool: incident notification and mitigation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@neuroretail.com>, ops@neuroretail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeuroRetail dedicated pool: incident notification and mitigation

Carlos / NeuroRetail ops team —

Quick heads-up: between 08:45 and 09:05 PT this morning we observed elevated eviction and queue depth on your dedicated GPU pool (pool-id: nr-dedicated-03) that caused token latencies to spike and a small percentage (~3.8%) of generation requests to return 503s or time out. Our automated fallback routed ~92% of affected traffic to the warm-standby nodes, which preserved most requests, but you may have seen degraded latency and a few failed calls during the window.

Immediate actions we took:
- Isolated the allocator instance that was showing a deadlock and restarted it (08:52 PT).
- Rebalanced the pool away from two noisy tenants to reduce headroom pressure (08:58 PT).
- Enabled an emergency temporary autoscale policy to add burst nodes to your pool while we gather evidence (09:03 PT).

Next steps we are working on now:
1) Collecting the support log bundle for your pool and application traces (attaching as soon as available).
2) A hotfix to prevent allocator deadlocks in this code path; engineering is on a focused patch.
3) Preparing a short post-incident summary and credit proposal by end of day Wednesday.

We understand the impact on your SLAs and are prioritizing this. If you have any immediate mitigation you want us to apply (e.g., route more traffic to region fallback, temporarily lower concurrency), tell us and we’ll action it now.

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll follow up with a timeline and the log bundle shortly.

—
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: (preparing) support_log_bundle_20270704.tar.gz (logs + traces)
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@neuroretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@neuroretail.com
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeuroRetail dedicated pool: incident notification and mitigation

Thanks, Evelyn —

We saw the spike on our side (a handful of customer chat sessions logged errors and a batch rerank job failed). Appreciate the quick routing to warm-standby. Two asks for now: 1) can you confirm whether any customer data or request payloads were retried/duplicated? 2) we will need the log bundle and a preliminary timeline for our incident review (preferably an ETA for the postmortem).

Also flagging that our procurement team will expect a credit estimate if this meets the SLA threshold.

Carlos
Head of Platform Ops | NeuroRetail
[carlos.ruiz@neuroretail.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NeuroRetail allocator deadlock findings and actions (internal)

Team —

Summary of preliminary findings from the support bundle (attached to internal drive):
- Root cause: an allocator deadlock triggered when two heavy fan-out jobs attempted concurrent prefix cache eviction during a hot-fanout window. The allocator’s lock ordering allowed a path where both silos waited on each other for ~14s, which caused queue-backpressure and cascaded into the autoscaler being unable to respond quickly enough.
- Impact: ~3.8% of requests returned 503/timeouts; tail latency for 95th increased from 220ms to 1.2s during peak; warm-standby handled the majority of traffic after reroute.

Immediate remediation we applied (already communicated to customer):
- Restarted offending allocator (Evelyn did this at 08:52).
- Emergency autoscale policy for burst nodes added (08:58).

Follow-up items (owner / ETA):
- Hotfix: change allocator lock ordering and add contention metrics (Jordan / 72h).
- Autoscaler tuning: decrease cooldown window under specific contention signals (Marissa / 5 business days).
- Customer communication: draft postmortem and credit proposal (Evelyn / Wed EOD).
- Short-term: implement a temporary per-tenant cap to avoid noisy-tenant amplifications (Ben / 48h).

Notes on customer-facing credit: prepare a credit that maps to SLA hit for the affected window; finance prefers a capped proposal with 1) service credit, 2) a one-time account credit that applied to next invoice. I’ll attach suggested numbers in the shared sheet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: NeuroRetail post-incident summary, evidence bundle, and proposed remediation

Carlos / team —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a short post-incident summary (redwood_postmortem_draft_20270707.pdf) and the support log bundle (support_log_bundle_20270704.tar.gz). High-level summary below and immediate asks.

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 08:44 PT — Short burst of high-fanout requests observed (neuro-session-1829).
- 08:45–08:52 PT — Allocator contention increases; requests start queuing and tail latency rises.
- 08:52 PT — Team isolated and restarted allocator instance (immediate drop in queue).
- 08:58 PT — Rebalanced tenants and added emergency autoscale burst; warm-standby absorbed remaining load.
- 09:03 PT — Stabilized; normal latencies restored by 09:10 PT.

Impact summary:
- Affected requests: ~3.8% of API calls during the 08:45–09:10 window saw elevated latency or failures.
- No evidence of payload duplication or data corruption in our traces; retries observed were at application layer (client-side). We have attached a trace map showing no duplicate write events.

Remediation and planned changes:
1) Hotfix to allocator lock ordering (Jordan) — target rollout in 72h to dedicated and warm-standby pools.
2) Autoscaler tuning and new contention signal (Marissa) — targeted in 5 business days with canary.
3) Short-term per-tenant concurrency cap (Ben) — deploy in 48h as a safety valve.
4) Improved observability: new contention metric exported to Console + alert (Ben / Marissa) — 2 business days.

Customer credit proposal:
- Proposed service credit: 25% prorated on the affected hourly usage for the pool during the incident window.
- One-time account credit: $12,000 applied to your next invoice to offset operational impact and investigation time.

Please let me know if you’d prefer an alternate credit structure; we can route the proposal to procurement/legal for formal sign-off.

Attached files:
- support_log_bundle_20270704.tar.gz (traces, allocator dumps, autoscaler logs)
- redwood_postmortem_draft_20270707.pdf (short post-incident writeup)
- account_credit_proposal_20270707.xlsx (breakdown of credit calc)

Carlos — would you like a joint runthrough of the postmortem for your execs? We can set a 30-min call tomorrow morning to walk through timeline and actions.

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll follow up once the hotfix is deployed and we’ve validated the canary.

—
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
